extracted.intended_audience: FDA employees, regulated industry, applicants/sponsors, media, and members of the public who participate in FDA administrative proceedings or guidance development
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures governing FDA advisory opinions, guidance documents (Good Guidance Practices), participation in outside standard-setting activities, public calendars, organizational representation, settlement proposals, and electronic media coverage of public administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes an advisory opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain written documents issued under this section constitute advisory opinions, including any portion of a Federal Register notice other than the text of a proposed or final regulation, trade correspondence issued by FDA between 1938 and 1946, compliance policy guides beginning in 1968 codified in the Compliance Policy Guides manual, and other documents specifically identified as advisory opinions (with examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific categories and examples of documents that, unless repudiated or overruled, will constitute advisory opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of advisory opinions (agency obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory opinion represents the formal position of FDA and, except as provided elsewhere, obligates the agency to follow it until it is amended or revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner may not recommend legal action against a person or product with respect to an action taken in conformity with an advisory opinion which has not been amended or revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for immediate significant danger to health
rubrics_metrics.description: In unusual situations involving an immediate and significant danger to health, the Commissioner may take appropriate civil enforcement action contrary to an advisory opinion before amending or revoking it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such action may be taken only with the approval of the Commissioner (non-delegable). Appropriate amendment or revocation of the advisory opinion will be expedited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment or revocation of advisory opinions; public notice and index
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory opinion may be amended or revoked at any time after issuance; notice of amendment or revocation will be given in the same manner as the original notice or in the Federal Register and will be placed on public display as part of the file in the Dockets Management Staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dockets Management Staff shall maintain a separate chronological index of all advisory opinions specifying the date of request, date of the opinion, and identification of the appropriate file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions taken in conformity with an advisory opinion after amendment/revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Action undertaken or completed in conformity with an advisory opinion that is later amended or revoked is acceptable to FDA unless the Commissioner determines substantial public interest considerations preclude continued acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever possible, an amended or revoked advisory opinion will state when prior actions do not remain acceptable and any applicable transition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment on advisory opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested person may submit written comments on an advisory opinion or modified advisory opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four copies of comments should be sent to the Dockets Management Staff for inclusion in the public file; individuals may submit only one copy. Comments will be considered in determining whether further modification is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of advisory opinions in proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory opinion may be used in administrative or court proceedings to illustrate acceptable and unacceptable procedures or standards, but not as a legal requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory opinions are illustrative, not binding legal requirements in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a statement is (or is not) an advisory opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement or advice by an FDA employee is an advisory opinion only if it is issued in writing under this section; oral statements or writings not under this section or §10.90 are informal communications and do not constitute advisory opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal communications represent the best judgment of the employee at that time but do not bind or obligate the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between regulations and guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA regulations are issued in the Federal Register and codified in the CFR; regulations may contain provisions enforced as legal requirements or intended only as guidance/recommendations, or both. Dissemination of draft notices and regulations is subject to §10.80.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text can be binding; guidance documents explain interpretation or policy and generally are nonbinding (see Good Guidance Practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations (non-regulatory) and their handling
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA issues recommendations (e.g., model ordinances, personnel practices) authorized by statute but not involving direct regulatory action; these may be handled under §10.115 procedures and are included in a separate public file of recommendations or published in the Federal Register as regulations under paragraph (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations may, at the Commissioner's discretion, follow GGP procedures but are tracked separately from guidance documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of agreements in public file
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal agreements, memoranda of understanding, or similar written documents executed by FDA and another person will be included in the public file on agreements established by the Division of Freedom of Information under §20.108.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A document not included in the public file is deemed rescinded and has no force or effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and encouragement of participation in outside standard-setting activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard-setting activities include development of performance characteristics, testing methodology, manufacturing practices, product standards, scientific protocols, compliance criteria, ingredient specifications, labeling, or other technical or policy criteria; FDA encourages employee participation in outside standard-setting activities that are in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of 'standard-setting' and states agency encouragement of participation subject to procedural controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval, documentation, and public file for Federal/state/international standard-setting participation
rubrics_metrics.description: An FDA employee may participate in standard-setting activities by other Federal agencies, State/local governments, UN organizations, international organizations, or foreign governments after approval under Staff Manual Guide procedures; approval forms and background information must be included in the public file on standard-setting activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability for public disclosure of records is governed by part 20; invitations to members of the public to present views will be extended to a representative sampling (consumer groups, industry, professional societies, academia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral responsibility of FDA liaison representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: An FDA employee appointed as liaison to an outside activity shall refer requests for information about or participation in the activity to the responsible group or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaison role is informational; the employee does not act as the organizer for public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for participation in private standard-setting activities
rubrics_metrics.description: An FDA employee may engage in private standard-setting activities after approval under Staff Manual Guide procedures; the requesting group must make a written request describing the scope and demonstrate that minimum standards (paragraph (d)(5)) are met. A granted request will be documented by a letter stating voting status, nonendorsement, and preclusion from serving as the deciding official if the standard later comes before FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request, approval form, and Commissioner's/center director's letter plus background information will be included in the public file; public disclosure governed by part 20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards for private standard-setting activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Private standard-setting activities in which FDA employees participate must: (i) be based on sound scientific and technological information, permit revision with new information, and protect the public against unsafe/ineffective/deceptive products or practices; (ii) not be designed for the economic benefit of any company/group or used for antitrust violations or establishment of certification/specific product approvals; and (iii) provide a procedure giving interested persons opportunity to provide information and views without payment of fees, with consideration of that input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization decides how the public input is provided (in person or in writing); FDA's involvement is contingent on these minimum standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership versus active participation in standard-setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership of an FDA employee in an organization that conducts standard-setting does not invoke the provisions of this section unless the employee participates in the standard-setting activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only active participation triggers the procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner exemption for particular standard-setting activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may determine in writing that direct FDA involvement in a particular activity is in the public interest and exempt the participation from certain requirements; the determination and justification will be included in the public file and relevant administrative file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include establishment/validation of analytical methods, drafting uniform laws/regulations, and development of public health recommendations by national/international organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for participation in certain associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of close cooperation and many agency employees' involvement, participation in activities of listed State/local government associations is exempt from most paragraph (d) requirements, except that a list of committees and groups of these associations will be included in the public file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a specified list (e.g., APHA, AAFCO, CF P, NABP, etc.) whose activities are treated as exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public calendar weekly preparation and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will prepare and make publicly available each week a public calendar showing, to the extent feasible, significant events of the previous week, including significant meetings with persons outside the executive branch involving designated FDA representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The calendar is to increase transparency about FDA interactions and significant agency events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items included and excluded on the public calendar
rubrics_metrics.description: Calendar entries will include significant meetings with judiciary/Congress when related to pending cases/hearings/regulatory actions, significant meetings/conferences/seminars/speeches, and social events sponsored by the regulated industry; the calendar will not include meetings that would prejudice law enforcement, invade privacy, meetings with the press, or meetings with onsite contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing openness with privacy and law enforcement needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calendar entry content and reporting responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For each calendar entry, the date, person(s), and subject matter involved will be specified; if many persons attend, names need not be specified. When more than one FDA representative attends, the most senior agency official will report the meeting on the public calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent reporting across events and identifies accountability for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officials required to be included on the public calendar
rubrics_metrics.description: The listed FDA representatives subject to this section include the Commissioner, Senior Associate Commissioners, Deputy Commissioners, Associate Commissioner for Regulatory Affairs, Center Directors, and Chief Counsel for the FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which agency officials' meetings are covered by the calendar requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public display locations for the public calendar
rubrics_metrics.description: The public calendar will be placed on public display at the Dockets Management Staff, the Office of the Associate Commissioner for Public Affairs, and on the FDA home page to the extent feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple points of public access are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation by an organization in administrative proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization may represent its members by filing petitions, comments, objections, and otherwise participating in administrative proceedings subject to this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows collective participation while clarifying rights of individual members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational participation does not abridge individual member rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition, comment, objection, or other representation by an organization will not abridge a member's right to take individual action of a similar type in the member's own name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves members' individual ability to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational annual member list request
rubrics_metrics.description: It is requested that each organization participating in FDA administrative proceedings file annually with the Dockets Management Staff a current list of all members of the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative transparency about organizational membership engaging with FDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of organizational filings for objections or requests for hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing by an organization of an objection or request for hearing under §§12.20–12.22 does not provide a member a legal right with respect to the objection or request for hearing that the member may individually exercise; a member wishing to file must do so individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that organizational filings do not substitute for an individual's procedural rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency position on class actions and preclusion in subsequent suits
rubrics_metrics.description: In a court proceeding in which an organization participates, the Commissioner will take measures to have the case brought or considered as a class action or otherwise binding upon all members except those specifically excluded by name; the Commissioner will take the position that issues are precluded from further litigation by members under collateral estoppel or res judicata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the agency's approach to organizational litigation and its effects on members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement proposals in proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time in the course of a proceeding, a person may propose settlement of the issues involved; participants will have an opportunity to consider proposed settlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unaccepted settlement proposals and related matters (e.g., proposed stipulations not agreed to) will not be admissible in evidence in an FDA administrative proceeding; FDA will oppose admission of settlement information in court or other administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Guidance Practices (GGPs) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Good guidance practices are FDA's policies and procedures for developing, issuing, and using guidance documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GGPs establish how guidance documents should be created, published, and managed to promote transparency and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance documents are prepared for FDA staff, applicants/sponsors, and the public to describe the agency's interpretation of or policy on a regulatory issue, and include documents related to design, production, labeling, promotion, manufacturing, testing, processing/evaluation/approval of submissions, and inspection/enforcement policies; they do not include certain excluded items (internal procedures, agency reports, consumer general information, speeches, journal articles, press materials, warning letters, MOUs, or communications directed to individual persons/firms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies what subject matter is appropriate for guidance documents and what is excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special terms: Level 1 and Level 2 guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Level 1 guidance documents: those that (i) set forth initial interpretations of statutory/regulatory requirements; (ii) set forth changes in interpretation/policy of more than a minor nature; (iii) include complex scientific issues; or (iv) cover highly controversial issues. Level 2 guidance documents: set forth existing practices or minor changes in interpretation/policy and include all guidance not classified as Level 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels determine the procedures FDA will follow in developing and issuing the guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding effect of guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable rights or responsibilities and do not legally bind the public or FDA; they represent the agency's current thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users may choose alternative approaches that comply with statutes and regulations; FDA employees may depart from guidance only with appropriate justification and supervisory concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using excluded documents to first communicate new regulatory expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may not use documents or means excluded from the definition of guidance document to informally communicate new or different regulatory expectations to a broad public audience for the first time; GGPs must be followed whenever regulatory expectations not readily apparent from statute/regulations are first communicated to a broad audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that new expectations are transmitted through proper guidance procedures to preserve notice and opportunity for comment when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for public participation in guidance development
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public can provide input on guidance documents under procedures in paragraph (g), suggest areas for guidance development (explaining why needed), submit draft guidance documents (marked 'Guidance Document Submission') to Dockets Management Staff or electronically to regulations.gov, suggest revisions or withdrawal of existing guidance (with reasons), comment on FDA's annual list of topics for possible guidance, and contact the responsible center or office to participate in development when FDA agrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides multiple avenues for stakeholders to engage in guidance development and revision; only one copy is necessary when submitting a draft and specific docket numbers or titles should be included for comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for development and issuance of Level 1 guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may seek early input before drafting; after preparing a draft Level 1 guidance, FDA will publish a notice in the Federal Register announcing availability, post the draft on the Internet and make hard copy available, and invite comment; FDA may also hold public meetings/workshops or present to advisory committees; after comment, FDA will review comments, prepare a final guidance incorporating changes when appropriate, publish a notice of availability in the Federal Register, post the guidance, and implement it. FDA may issue another draft if appropriate and repeat steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior public participation is not feasible or appropriate, FDA may implement without seeking comment but will still publish and invite comments and revise as appropriate after receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for immediate implementation of guidance when prior participation not feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA determines prior public participation is not feasible or appropriate for a Level 1 guidance, it will publish a notice that the guidance is available, post and make it available in hard copy, immediately implement the guidance, and invite comment upon issuance; comments will be reviewed and the guidance revised when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows for expedited implementation while still inviting subsequent public comment and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for development and issuance of Level 2 guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: After preparing a Level 2 guidance, FDA will post it on the Internet and make hard copy available, immediately implement it unless indicated otherwise when made available, and invite public comment; comments will be reviewed and revisions posted when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 2 uses a streamlined process acknowledging that these documents set forth existing practices or minor changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to comment on guidance at any time and comment submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You can comment on any guidance document at any time. Comments under paragraph (g) must be sent to Dockets Management Staff with the docket number or title identified; comments will be made available to the public under the agency's submission rules in §10.20(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the procedural details for where and how to submit comments and how they will be handled publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of a guidance document and prohibited language
rubrics_metrics.description: A guidance document must include the term 'guidance,' identify the issuing center(s)/office(s), identify the activity and people to whom it applies, prominently display a statement of nonbinding effect, include the date of issuance, note if it revises a previous guidance (and identify the replaced document), and contain the word 'draft' if it is a draft. Guidance documents must not include mandatory language such as 'shall,' 'must,' 'required,' or 'requirement' unless describing a statutory or regulatory requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures clarity about the document's status, applicability, and nonbinding nature; limited exception for international negotiation drafts for draft stage only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval authority within FDA for issuing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each center and office must have written procedures for the approval of guidance documents that ensure issuance is approved by appropriate senior FDA officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centers/offices must document internal approval processes to ensure senior official concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and revision of existing guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will periodically review existing guidance documents to determine whether they need to be changed or withdrawn and will review/revise guidance when significant changes are made to statute or regulations; members of the public may suggest revisions or withdrawals at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous review process to keep guidance current with law and policy changes and responsive to public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring FDA staff compliance with GGPs
rubrics_metrics.description: All current and new FDA employees involved in guidance development, issuance, or application will be trained on the GGPs; centers and offices will monitor development and issuance to ensure GGPs are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training and monitoring are the agency's internal controls to enforce adherence to GGPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to guidance documents and notification of availability
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will make copies of guidance documents available in hard copy and, as feasible, through the Internet; FDA will maintain an internet list of all guidance documents, add new documents within 30 days of issuance, and publish an annual comprehensive list in the Federal Register identifying additions or withdrawals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance lists will include the name of the document, issuance/revision dates, and information on obtaining copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies if an FDA staff member fails to follow GGPs
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe someone at FDA did not follow the GGPs or treated a guidance as binding, you should contact that person's supervisor, and if unresolved, contact the next highest supervisor or the center/office ombudsman; if still unresolved, ask the Office of the Chief Mediator and Ombudsman to become involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a chain-of-command and ombudsman process to address alleged departures from GGPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for electronic media coverage guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'public administrative proceeding' (any FDA proceeding the public has a right to attend), 'advance notice' (written/telephone notice to Office of Public Affairs of intent to electronically record), and 'electronic recording' (visual or audio recording made by videotape/film or other electronic means).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes terms used for media coverage procedures in Subpart C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy of openness and advance notice for electronic media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA policy favors openness and making public administrative proceedings more accessible; because electronic coverage presents difficulties, FDA requests advance notice of intent to record to facilitate orderly conduct and allow presiding officers to make special arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline will be referred to in Federal Register notices so parties know proceedings may be recorded and established procedures exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer discretion over electronic coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The designated presiding officer retains discretionary authority (from other regulating parts) to regulate conduct and electronic coverage to ensure timely, fair, and orderly hearings; the guideline sets procedures presiding officers should ordinarily follow but allows departure in particular situations under the presumption of openness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretion to limit coverage is to be exercised only in unusual circumstances; room design and hearing duration may allow less restrictive approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure of proceedings to electronic media when closed to public
rubrics_metrics.description: If a portion or all of a proceeding is closed to the public because material is not disclosable under law, the proceeding will also be closed to electronic media coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency between public access and media coverage—closed sessions remain closed to recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool sharing and representation when space is limited for media
rubrics_metrics.description: If space limitations preclude many cameras, the presiding officer may require pool sharing; pool sharing arrangements for resulting tape should be made among those allowed to film and those excluded, and FDA is committed to ensuring non-major networks can obtain a copy at cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency expects media representatives to negotiate agreements before proceedings; if no agreement, agency will use time of advance notice receipt to determine representation (e.g., one network reporter, one independent reporter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency determination of media representation when no agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agreement among media cannot be reached before the proceeding, FDA will use the time of receipt of advance notice to determine representation for each category of media and may designate who records (e.g., one network, one independent reporter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an objective basis (time of notice) for allocating limited recording opportunities and encourages prior negotiation among media.
